text: When Adoni-zedek king of Jerusalem heard that Joshua had captured Ai and devoted it to destruction, doing to Ai and its king as he had done to Jericho and its king, and that the inhabitants of Gibeon had made peace with Israel and were living among them,
Adoni-zedek and his people were terrified, for Gibeon was a great city, like one of the royal cities—larger than Ai—and all its men were warriors.

versions.text: he was terrified, for Gibeon was a great city, like one of the royal cities—larger than Ai—and all its men were warriors.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew verb וַיִּֽירְאוּ is plural ("they feared greatly"), indicating the king together with his people, not the king alone. The singular "he was terrified" loses this element of the text.

text: So Adoni-zedek king of Jerusalem sent word to Hoham king of Hebron, Piram king of Jarmuth, Japhia king of Lachish, and Debir king of Eglon:
"Come up to me and help me, and let us attack Gibeon, for it has made peace with Joshua and the Israelites."

Then the five kings of the Amorites—the kings of Jerusalem, Hebron, Jarmuth, Lachish, and Eglon—joined forces and marched up with all their armies. They took up positions against Gibeon and attacked it.

The men of Gibeon sent word to Joshua at the camp in Gilgal: "Do not abandon your servants. Come up to us quickly, save us, and help us, for all the Amorite kings of the hill country have joined forces against us."
So Joshua marched up from Gilgal with his whole army, all his best fighting men.
And the LORD said to Joshua, "Do not be afraid of them, for I have given them into your hand. Not one of them will be able to stand against you."
Joshua came upon them suddenly, having marched all night from Gilgal.
The LORD threw them into confusion before Israel, who struck them down in a great slaughter at Gibeon, pursued them along the road up to Beth-horon, and cut them down as far as Azekah and Makkedah.

As they fled before Israel down the descent of Beth-horon, the LORD hurled great hailstones on them from the sky all the way to Azekah, and they died. More of them died from the hailstones than from the swords of the Israelites.
On the day the LORD gave the Amorites over to the Israelites, Joshua spoke to the LORD, and in the sight of Israel he said: "Sun, stand still over Gibeon, and moon, over the Valley of Aijalon."

So the sun stood still and the moon halted until the nation had taken vengeance on its enemies. Is this not written in the Book of Jashar?* The sun stopped in the middle of the sky and delayed its setting for about a full day. [*Footnote: Jashar means "the upright one"; the book is an ancient collection of songs no longer preserved.]

versions.text: So the sun stood still and the moon halted until the nation had taken vengeance on its enemies. Is this not written in the Book of Jashar? The sun stopped in the middle of the sky and delayed its setting for about a full day.
versions.explanation: A brief footnote explaining the unfamiliar name "Jashar" would help hearers, since the reference is to a lost source unknown to most listeners.

text: There has never been a day like it before or since, a day when the LORD listened to the voice of a man—because the LORD was fighting for Israel.
Then Joshua returned with all Israel to the camp at Gilgal.
Now the five kings had fled and hidden in the cave at Makkedah.
When Joshua was told, "The five kings have been found, hiding in the cave at Makkedah,"
he said, "Roll large stones up to the mouth of the cave, and post men there to guard them.
But you—do not stop. Pursue your enemies and attack them from behind. Do not let them reach their cities, for the LORD your God has given them into your hand."
When Joshua and the Israelites had finished inflicting a crushing defeat on them, until they were wiped out—though a few survivors escaped to the fortified cities—
the whole army returned safely to Joshua at the camp in Makkedah, and no one dared say a word against the Israelites.
Then Joshua said, "Open the mouth of the cave and bring those five kings out to me."
So they did, bringing the five kings out of the cave to him—the kings of Jerusalem, Hebron, Jarmuth, Lachish, and Eglon.

When they had brought these kings to Joshua, he summoned all the men of Israel and said to the commanders of the troops who had gone with him, "Come here, put your feet on the necks of these kings." So they came forward and put their feet on their necks.
Joshua said to them, "Do not be afraid or dismayed. Be strong and courageous, for this is what the LORD will do to all the enemies you fight."
Then Joshua struck the kings down and killed them, and hung them on five trees, where they remained until evening.

At sunset Joshua gave the order, and they took them down from the trees and threw them into the cave where they had been hiding. Then they placed large stones over the mouth of the cave, and those stones remain there to this very day.

versions.text: At sunset Joshua gave the order, and they took them down from the trees and threw them into the cave where they had been hiding. Then they placed large stones over the mouth of the cave, and they are there to this very day.
versions.explanation: "They are there" is ambiguous when read aloud—it could be heard as referring to the kings rather than the stones. Naming the stones explicitly matches the Hebrew sense and reads more clearly.

text: That day Joshua captured Makkedah and put it and its king to the sword. He devoted the city and everyone in it to destruction, leaving no survivor, and he did to the king of Makkedah as he had done to the king of Jericho.
Then Joshua and all Israel with him moved on from Makkedah to Libnah and attacked it.

The LORD gave that city and its king into Israel's hand as well. Joshua put it to the sword along with everyone in it, leaving no survivor there, and he did to its king as he had done to the king of Jericho.
Then Joshua and all Israel with him moved on from Libnah to Lachish. He laid siege to it and attacked it.
The LORD gave Lachish into Israel's hand, and Joshua captured it on the second day. He put it to the sword along with everyone in it, just as he had done to Libnah.
Then Horam king of Gezer came up to help Lachish, but Joshua struck him down along with his people, until no survivor was left.
Then Joshua and all Israel with him moved on from Lachish to Eglon. They laid siege to it and attacked it.
They captured it that very day and put it to the sword, devoting to destruction everyone in it, just as they had done to Lachish.

versions.text: They captured it that same day and put it to the sword, devoting to destruction everyone in it that day, just as they had done to Lachish.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew repeats "on that day," but doubling it in English ("that same day... that day") stumbles when read aloud. Keeping the time reference once preserves the sense and improves the rhythm.

text: Then Joshua and all Israel with him went up from Eglon to Hebron and attacked it.

They captured it and put it to the sword, along with its king, all its towns, and everyone in it. They left no survivor, just as they had done to Eglon; they devoted the city and everyone in it to destruction.

versions.text: They captured it and put it to the sword, along with its king, its villages, and everyone in it. They left no survivor, just as they had done to Eglon; they devoted the city and everyone in it to destruction.
versions.explanation: "עָרֶיהָ" means its (dependent) cities or towns; "all its towns" better reflects the Hebrew term and also renders the inclusive "כָּל" (all), which is currently unrepresented.

text: Then Joshua and all Israel with him turned back to Debir and attacked it.

They captured it, its king, and all its villages, and put them to the sword. They devoted everyone in it to destruction, leaving no survivor. Joshua did to Debir and its king as he had done to Hebron and to Libnah and its king.

So Joshua struck down the whole land—the hill country, the Negev, the western foothills, and the slopes—together with all their kings. He left no survivor but devoted everything that breathed to destruction, as the LORD, the God of Israel, had commanded.
Joshua conquered them from Kadesh-barnea to Gaza, and the whole region of Goshen as far as Gibeon.
All these kings and their lands Joshua captured in one campaign, because the LORD, the God of Israel, fought for Israel.
Then Joshua returned with all Israel to the camp at Gilgal.
